title.narrative: Scaling up HIV prevention, care and treatment services for Key Populations and People living with HIV in Kosovo, and Strengthening Tuberculosis ("TB") control in Kosovo

description.narrative: Kosovo - TB/HIV - Community Development Fund - CDF. This program has the following goals: To maintain low prevalence of HIV among general population and key populations and improve the quality of life of people affected by AIDS in Kosovo. To reduce the overall incidence of notified cases from 33.8 per 100,000 in 2019 to 23.6 per 100,000 in 2024 and maintain tuberculosis mortality in Kosovo below 1.5/100,000.. The objectives of this program are: Reduce the impact of HIV in general population and key populations by strengthening HIV prevention interventions and improve access to services. Improve the health status and quality of life of people living with HIV by providing universal access to treatment, health care and other support services. Ensure sustainable response to HIV through strengthening coordination, leadership and financial and political commitment of the Government. Ensure sustainable response to HIV through resilient health systems strengthening interventions. Empowerment and engagement of CSO in HIV policy, programming, advocacy and HIV services in the community through CSS. Successfully treat all cases of tuberculosis and maintain at least 85% the treatment success rate.. Strengthen the early prevention and detection of tuberculosis by intensifying the active and passive findings of the cases by providing quality services and adequate measures of infection control and LTBI treatment of cases and other ongoing support.. Establish and support national-level policies and legal framework and ensure greater government political and financial commitment to effective TB response in Kosovo. Improving patient-centred tuberculosis care through increased CSO engagement and strengthening public-private partnership. Improve national capacity to investigate and assess the impact of tuberculosis control and pre-elimination of interventions.
